extracted.intended_audience: Users of SINGULAR (computational algebra / algebraic geometry researchers) who use the gitfan.lib library
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of procedures in the SINGULAR gitfan.lib for computing GIT fans, orbit cones, moving cones, and symmetry actions; meant to guide users in invoking these procedures and understanding their inputs/outputs and notes. Includes usage forms, purposes, returns, notes and examples for each procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: GITfan
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GITfan(J,Q [, G]); J:ideal, Q:intmat, G:list. Purpose: Computes the GIT fan associated to J and Q. Optionally a symmetry group action on the column space of Q can be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a fan, the GIT fan. Note: The proceduce uses parallel computation for the construction of the GIT-cones. The a-faces are not computed in parallel. This can be done by calling the aface procedure specifying a list of simplex faces. If used with the optional argument G, the orbit decomposition of the simplex of columns of Q is computed. Refer to the Singular documentation on how to do this more efficiently using GAP. Example provided (setcores, ring, ideal J, intmat Q, fan GIT = GITfan(J,Q); and example with symmetry group: fan GIT2 = GITfan(J,Q,simplexSymmetryGroup)).

rubrics_metrics.name: GITfanFromOrbitCones
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GITfanFromOrbitCones(OC, Q, Qgamma [, file1, file2]); OC:list, Q:bigintmat, Qgamma:cone, file1:string, file2:string. Purpose: Returns the common refinement of the cones given in the list OC which is supposed to contain the orbit cones intersected with Qgamma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a list containing the bigint hashes of the GIT cones. Note: The optional argument can be used to specify one or two strings with file names, where the first file will contain the hashes of the GIT-cones and the second argument the actual cones in their H-representation. To obtain the whole GIT-fan Qgamma has to be take the cone generated by the columns of Q. Example shows building AF, OC, Qgamma = coneViaPoints(transpose(Q)), list GIT = GITfanFromOrbitCones(OC,Q,Qgamma); size(GIT) -> 76.

rubrics_metrics.name: GITfanParallel
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GITfanParallel(OC, Q, Qgamma [, file1]); OC:list, Q:intmat, Qgamma:cone, file1:string. Purpose: Returns the common refinement of the cones given in the list OC which is supposed to contain the orbit cones intersected with Qgamma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a list containing the bigint hashes of the GIT cones. Note: The proceduce uses parallel computation for the construction of the GIT-cones. The optional argument can be used to specify a name for a file which will contain the hashes of the GIT-cones. Example demonstrates setcores(4) and computing size(GIT) -> 76.

rubrics_metrics.name: GKZfan
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from library gitfan.lib (listed as D.15.16.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No detailed usage/purpose/return block is present in this chunk; entry indicates the procedure exists in the library (GKZfan).

rubrics_metrics.name: movingCone
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: movingCone(Q); Q: intmat. Purpose: Computes the moving cone from the grading matrix, with the degrees in the columns of Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a cone. Example shows computing cone mov = movingCone(Q); printing mov yields AMBIENT_DIM, FACETS, LINEAR_SPAN, and rays(mov) output; example facets and rays are shown. Use when you need to restrict orbit cones to the moving cone or to inspect the moving cone structure from Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: computeAfaceOrbits
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: computeAfaceOrbits(AF,G); AF list of intvecs, G: list of permutations. Purpose: Computes the orbits of the afaces in the list AF under the group action in G, where G is a list of permutations. We assume that the elements of G form a group and the first entry corresponds to the neutral element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a list of lists of intvecs. Example shows building simplexSymmetryGroup = G25Action(), generating simplexOrbitRepresentatives, calling afaces(J,simplexOrbitRepresentatives), and then computeAfaceOrbits(...); apply(afaceOrbits,size) returns e.g. '10 15 10 1' for sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: minimalAfaceOrbits
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minimalAfaceOrbits(afaceOrbits); afaceOrbits: list. Purpose: Returns a list of all minimal a-face orbits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a list of intvecs. Example demonstrates building afaceOrbits and then list minAfaceOrbits = minimalAfaceOrbits(afaceOrbits); apply(minAfaceOrbits,size) -> outputs like '10 15'. Use to reduce aface orbit lists to minimal representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: orbitConeOrbits
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: orbitConeOrbits(F, Q); F: list, Q: intmat. Purpose: Projects a list F of a-face orbits to the orbit cones with respect to Q. The function checks whether the projections are of full dimension and returns an error otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a list of lists of cones. Note: Example shows preparing simplexOrbitRepresentatives, computing afaceOrbits, then minAfaceOrbits = minimalAfaceOrbits(...), and finally list listOfOrbitConeOrbits = orbitConeOrbits(minAfaceOrbits,Q). Use this to convert aface orbits into orbit-cones (and ensure full-dimensionality).

rubrics_metrics.name: minimalOrbitConeOrbits
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minimalOrbitConeOrbits(listOfOrbits); listOfOrbits: list of lists of cones. Purpose: Minimizes a list of orbit cone orbits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a list of lists of cones. Example shows creating listOfOrbitConeOrbits and calling minimalOrbitConeOrbits(listOfOrbitConeOrbits); size(listOfMinimalOrbitConeOrbits) -> 2 in example. Use to remove redundant orbit-cone orbits and obtain minimal set.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersectOrbitsWithMovingCone
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: intersectOrbitsWithMovingCone(OCmin, mov); OCmin: list of lists of cones, mov: cone. Purpose: Intersects all cones in the orbits in OCmin with mov discarting all orbits of cones which are not of full dimension. The resulting orbits are duplicate free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a list of lists of cones. Example workflow: compute AF, afaceOrbits, minAfaceOrbits, listOfOrbitConeOrbits = orbitConeOrbits(...), cone mov = movingCone(Q); then intersectOrbitsWithMovingCone(listOfOrbitConeOrbits,mov) yields filtered orbits (example prints FACETS etc). Use to restrict orbit cones to the moving cone and remove non-full-dimension or duplicate orbits.

rubrics_metrics.name: groupActionOnQImage
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: groupActionOnQImage(G,Q); G: list of permutations, Q: intmat. Purpose: Given the group G of permutations acting on the simplex on ncols(Q) objects, computes the corresponding group action on the image of Q. We assume that the basering has characteristic 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list of matrices. Example: given generatorsG (permutations), calling groupActionOnQImage(generatorsG,Q) returns a list of matrices representing the group action on the Q-image. Use when you want the linear representation of a permutation group acting on column-space of Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: groupActionOnHashes
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: groupActionOnHashes(Asigma,OCmov); Asigma: list, OCmov: list of list of cones. Purpose: From the list of orbits of orbitcones, and the symmetry group represenation given by the matrices in Asigma, compute the corresponding permutation representation of the symmetry group on the orbit cones. The permutations are speciﬁed in a map representation of length the sum of the size of the orbits of OCmov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list of permutations. Example shows building Asigmagens = groupActionOnQImage(generatorsG,Q) and then groupActionOnHashes(Asigmagens,list(OC)); output is a list (map) of permutations describing group action on hashes/orbit-cones. Use to obtain permutation action on computed GIT-cones/orbit-cones for symmetry exploitation and orbit-finding.
